title: MyRecon vs Epieos: Handle vs Email OSINT | MyRecon
description: Compare MyRecon handle sweeps, breach checks and DNS tools with Epieos reverse email and phone lookups, pricing tiers and source limits.
h1: MyRecon vs Epieos: handle sweeps vs email OSINT
intro: Epieos specializes in reverse email and phone investigations, pivoting from an address into linked Google account metadata and Holehe-style service registrations. MyRecon begins with multi-platform handle sweeps while also offering free email breach lookups, k-anonymity password checks, and domain DNS tools. Both solve distinct starting points.

sections.heading: Email-first pivoting versus handle-first discovery
sections.body: When your only clue is an email address or phone number, Epieos checks over 140 connected services and public Google artifacts such as contributor reviews or Gravatar records. When you start with an alias or want to audit handles across 560+ platforms plus email breaches, MyRecon covers the wider handle surface.

link.label: Compare free email OSINT tools for self-audits

sections.heading: Access tiers, pricing and free usage limits
sections.body: Epieos restricts anonymous visitors to three captcha-gated searches before requiring paid subscriptions (such as its Osinter tier around EUR 29.99 per month for 30 requests). MyRecon gives guests unlimited free email breach lookups, five daily Quick handle previews, and five daily Standard 560+ scans upon free sign-in.

sections.heading: How MyRecon handles email and contributor signals
sections.body: MyRecon's email lookup runs free for guests without touching username scan quotas, keeping optional linked-account lookups switched off by default until you opt in. Inside Deep Search, email queries can also retrieve public Google contributor metadata while keeping unavailable providers clearly flagged as incomplete rather than clean.

sections.heading: Privacy boundaries and source verification
sections.body: Neither platform unlocks private mailboxes, passwords, or non-public messages. With Epieos, registration probes infer whether an address signed up on third-party sites; with MyRecon, breach records reflect historical corpus disclosures. Always confirm ownership directly through official login recovery before closing accounts.

faq.question: Can MyRecon replace Epieos for reverse phone lookups?
faq.answer: No. MyRecon intentionally does not offer phone-number-to-name lookups. If your investigation starts strictly from a phone number, Epieos or dedicated carrier-validation workflows cover a different input.

faq.question: Why are MyRecon email breach checks free without a captcha quota?
faq.answer: MyRecon queries LeakCheck and XposedOrNot for public breach exposure and keeps optional linked-account probes opt-in, leaving email checks free for guests without consuming handle scan allowances.

faq.question: Does Epieos sweep hundreds of sites for a social handle?
faq.answer: No. Epieos centers on reverse email and phone footprinting across roughly 140 services, whereas MyRecon sweeps 100 to 3,000+ platforms starting from a handle.

faq.question: Which option suits personal security and breach audits?
faq.answer: MyRecon combines free email breach history, k-anonymity password exposure checks, domain MX/SPF/DMARC diagnostics, and handle discovery in one toolkit, making it practical for routine self-audits.
